title: Saudi-Houthi Conflict Escalates in Yemen: Riyadh Airport Attack, Oil Facility Attacks
summary: Saudi-led coalition launched strikes on Houthi-controlled Hodeidah governorate, while Houthi groups accuse attacks of escalating tensions in Yemen. Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabian cities, wounding over 70 people and setting oil facilities ablaze, with Saudi Arabia promising retaliation. The attacks also led to a deadly Houthi missile attack on the Riyadh airport, killing 13 people and injuring over 300.

facts.statement: Saudi-led coalition launched strikes on Houthi-controlled Hodeidah governorate in Yemen.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabian cities, killing over 70 people.
The attacks on the Saudi capital airport and oil facilities led to casualties and infrastructure damage.

sources.title: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’
sources.description:
Ukrainian president earlier rejected US call for Kyiv to stop bombing oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end attacks on energy infrastructure

  • US politics – live updates

Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”.

In a social media post, the US president claimed the two sides had reached an agreement. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” he wrote on Truth Social.

Continue reading...

sources.title: Trump’s deal with Putin will have little impact on US diesel prices, experts say
sources.description:
Analysts say fuel will take weeks to ship and quantity is too small to affect prices, while full deal is unlikely to be met given damage to Russian refineries

  • Trump announces partial ceasefire but Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’

Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on US imports of Russian diesel will have little “meaningful” effect on motorists and businesses in the US and overseas, energy and foreign policy analysts have predicted.

The US president infuriated Volodymyr Zelenskyy when he announced the deal on Friday, writing on Truth Social that the agreement with his Russia counterpart to supply millions of tonnes of diesel was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared after his decision to go to war against Iran.

Continue reading...

sources.title: Middle East crisis live: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim responsibility for attack that killed 12
sources.description:
Statement claims strikes against Dammam airport and Saudi Aramco facilities but it is unclear if group also claims today’s reported attack

Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace.

In a significant message, the United Arab Emirates has issued a statement in solidarity with Saudi Arabia – expressing support for “all measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom’s security and stability”.

The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.

Continue reading...

sources.title: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi-led coalition says
sources.description:
Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid airport as escalating attacks threaten to draw more countries into Yemen conflict

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

  • Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy

A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people.

An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire and causing injuries, according to the Saudi authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week.

Continue reading...

sources.title: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport forces swift rethink of Trump’s new strategy
sources.description:
US president’s plan to park the wars in Iran and Yemen, while blaming Ukraine for diesel prices, looks unsustainable

  • Middle East crisis live - latest updates

The reckless missile attack on King Khalid international airport in Riyadh on Saturday did not just export the death and misery inside Yemen to Saudi Arabia, it also left Donald Trump forced to reconsider his diplomatic and political strategy designed to take him into the midterm elections next month.

The US president’s plan had only been unveiled on Friday. He said it was the result of “a world problem” – spiralling diesel prices – which he blamed on Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. He was going to keep the political temperature down on his war of choice in Iran and its spillover in Yemen until after the midterms.

Continue reading...

sources.title: Zelenskyy signals support for Russia-Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire’ after surprise Trump announcement – live updates
sources.description:
Ukraine’s president reportedly says Kyiv would accept a deal if Moscow does after US president posts announcement with no detail on social media

  • Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

The president of the EU Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, has expressed her “full support for President Zelenskyy” amid calls for a ceasefire.

In a telephone call with the Ukrainian leader, von der Leyen posted on X that she “fully supported the call of President Zelenskyy for a ceasefire that would protect global food supplies and energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia.

“Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it’s important for Russia to support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side. From our Ukrainian side, there is always FULL support for de-escalation steps, protection of lives, and the necessary decisions to end the war and ensure lasting peace.”

Continue reading...

sources.title: India condemns attack on Saudi airport that killed 12, injured over 300
sources.description:
India on Sunday strongly condemned a major attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured over 300.
New Delhi said the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Gulf nation are "completely unacceptable and must cease immediately."
"We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.
"We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons," it said.
Saudi Arabia has blamed Houthi militants for the attack.
"We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.
